scope: Offline review only; no device access, kernel change, or active-attempt intervention

basis: The actual native KC inspector resolves all five selected globals inside loaded non-executable segments.
The captured bootstrap FP resolves inside the actual KC __BOOTDATA segment. The bounded 8192-byte read covers the 256-byte early-panic buffer.
Read commands require an owned paused callback and remain on its existing proxy reader. No pointer chasing, guest continuation, reset, or reboot is introduced.
The physical mapping calculation agrees with the attempt002 BootArgs-derived slide. EL12 values are additional observations, not an automatic explanation of the panic.

later_evidence_preservation_followups.finding: stop() saves self.raw and self.event after diagnostic proxy commands. Pinned proxy.reply() can dispatch a nested REQ_BOOT while awaiting a reply; dispatch() resets these fields before stop() detects reentrance. Catching BoundedStop alone does not preserve the original event/context in that path.
later_evidence_preservation_followups.action: Snapshot the original raw bytes, event, and context error before diagnostic I/O; use those immutable locals for the final record. Reject nested boot dispatch while stopping before it mutates the original fields. Add a host-only nested-callback regression.

later_evidence_preservation_followups.finding: Partial globals are assigned to result only after the entire loop, and EL12 values only after the dictionary comprehension completes. Any EL12 failure skips the later stack read.
later_evidence_preservation_followups.action: Attach result dictionaries before incremental reads. Capture the bounded stack before optional EL12 observations so a register-read failure cannot discard the primary panic evidence.

attempt002_panic_analysis.confirmed: The exact linked call at panic_trap_to_debugger+0x98 enters panic_spin_forever from the PE_kputc == NULL early-panic branch. Normal debugger_panic_* globals are not populated on this branch.
attempt002_panic_analysis.leading_cause: Bootloader entropy length mismatch, strongly supported but awaiting the formatted stack message and saved caller.
evidence: The captured x6 minus the supplied slide equals bootseed_init_bootloader+0x74, the exact return address of its insufficient-entropy panic call. The compiled panic wrapper puts its caller in x6.
prng_random.c:51-75 requires 4 * SHA512_DIGEST_LENGTH = 256 bootloader seed bytes on ARM64.
The saved real original ADT contains /chosen/random-seed with length 64. Only its property length was inspected for this review; seed bytes were not printed or copied into the report.
pe_gen.c:145-216 returns the available seed length, zeroing consumed ADT bytes; it returns zero for an all-zero seed. The exact actual returned count is not yet established.
arm_vm_init.c:1894 invokes early_random for the physical-aperture slide before serial initialization; earlier early_random consumers are also possible without a saved frame chain.
attempt002_panic_analysis.recommended_loader_fix_if_confirmed: Supply exactly 256 fresh bytes from the M5 OS CSPRNG in the guest-only /chosen/random-seed property before final ADT serialization. Preserve the original ADT privately, verify byte-property roundtrip and capacity, and retain the kernel entropy checks. Do not expand the original 64 bytes deterministically or reuse a prior attempt's seed. Record source and byte count, not seed values. No kernel rebuild is required.
not_inferred: UART FAR is not evidence that UART caused the panic.
Early panic is not arm_vm_init completion, command-line success, or full OS boot.
Attempt003 has not been observed by this reviewer; root owns execution and recovery.
